receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for forwarding your draft Share Purchase Agreement. We have several substantive points to discuss:

1. Price: Based on our diligence and market conditions, our client cannot accept the current $45,000,000 price. We propose a revised purchase price of $33,000,000, subject to customary adjustment mechanisms for debt, cash, and working capital at closing.

2. Seller Representations: The seller’s warranty regarding the financial statements is insufficient. We require an expanded suite of representations and warranties as to (a) compliance with GAAP, (b) full disclosure of liabilities, (c) existence and enforceability of all material contracts, (d) title to shares, and (e) compliance with applicable law.

3. Escrow: To secure the post-closing risk, at least 15% of the consideration should be placed in escrow for 18 months.

4. Closing: The proposed 30-day closing period may be too short given due diligence requirements. Please confirm if there is flexibility here.

We look forward to your revised draft incorporating these points and will provide further comments on receipt.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

probe.private_reasoning: The Seller’s initial price was USD 45m and quickly dropped by USD 6m (13.3%) after only one Buyer counter. They showed willingness to move further, and their comment invites more negotiation on liability caps—implying room for flexibility, especially if favorable deal terms are offered. There is no evidence in comments, metadata, or hidden text suggesting a hard floor. This pattern usually signals a bottom line materially lower than the current ask. It’s likely their client will accept significantly less, as the speed and size of the concession signals a desire to transact. However, the Seller will want to show resistance before dropping further. My best estimate is USD 36m, representing a further 7.7% drop, which matches typical negotiation behavior when the Seller is keen but wants to ensure concessions are exchanged for terms.
